newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices fall on new crop arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices fall on new crop arrivals.

text.p: Cotton prices suffered a setback at the improved level on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Mill demand was at low ebb while new crop arrivals triggered fresh selling," a dealer said.
Farmers are now bringing more cotton to the market as rains have stopped, traders said.
In spot deals, Bengal-deshi slid by 35 rupees to 885/925 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), while Punjab saw-ginned fell to 1,590/1,750 rupees from 1,615/1,800 rupees per maund.
Long-staple Gujarat Sankar-4 fell to 20,500/20,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) from 20,700/21,300 rupees. November delivery was quoted lower at 19,850/19,900 rupees per candy.
